b: An earlier draft of Field Manual IV quoted John D. Rockefeller as saying that the ability to keep your head when all others are losing theirs was a competitive edge. That phrasing is Rudyard Kipling's, from “If—” (1895). I could find no reliable attribution of it to Rockefeller. The point about his temperament stands; the quotation is gone.

I had repeated the standard story that John Snow removed the pump handle and stopped the 1854 outbreak. Whitehead's own figures show fatal attacks had already fallen from 142 on 1 September to 14 by the 8th, the day the handle came off, and Snow never claimed otherwise. The entry now says what the evidence says.

I had written that Harrison was finally paid the longitude prize in 1773. He received £8,750 from Parliament that year and £23,065 in total across all sources — but the statutory £20,000 was never awarded, to him or to anyone.
An early draft said roughly 6,000 miles of British railway were authorised at the peak. The 1846 figure is about 9,500 miles across 263 Acts.

Silicon & Light said an international consortium began work on extreme ultraviolet lithography in 1997. The 1997 consortium, EUV LLC, was American: Intel, AMD and Motorola with three US national laboratories. ASML was admitted in 1999, and that is when the programme became international.

The Great Divergence printed '3' as a figure — the explanations still standing. It was my own count, not a sourced number, and the entry itself discusses more than three. It is replaced by Robert Allen's estimate of the return on a spinning jenny: 38% in England against 2.5% in France.

The Unix Bargain dated the rewrite of Unix in C to 1972 and called C a language invented so the system could move. Ritchie's own account puts the kernel rewrite in the summer of 1973 and says portability carried little weight at the time; it became the point with the 1977 port to the Interdata 8/32. The entry also said Thompson wrote the first version in three weeks. By his own account it took the month his wife and son were away.

t: A source that did not exist.
b: The Banking Model of Education listed a Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy entry on Paulo Freire in its reading list. The Stanford Encyclopedia has no entry on Freire; he appears only inside other articles. The reading list now points to the Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy's entry, which does exist. The link had been dead since publication.

t: Six lives said more than their sources.
b: A sourcing pass opened the documents behind the figures in eight lives, and six said more than those documents do. Fritz Haber said roughly half the nitrogen in your body came through his process and that three to four billion people are alive because of it. The first line was found in no document opened. The study most often cited gives 48 per cent of the world's population in 2008, and the entry now says that. John D. Rockefeller put Standard Oil's ninety per cent of American refining in the early 1880s; the source opened puts it at 1879. Andrew Carnegie called the 1901 sale the largest transaction in industrial history; neither source opened says so, and the sentence now says what they do. Robert Moses gave thirteen bridges and hundreds of playgrounds as Caro's count; only the $27 billion was found. Steve Jobs said he paid Lucasfilm for its graphics group; by Alvy Ray Smith's account the new company paid for the technology out of Jobs's ten million. Tu Youyou's sixty laboratories are sixty institutions in the WHO's count. Each figure now carries the document it was read in.

The Banking Model of Education said Freire's workers at Angicos learned to read in forty-five days, and printed 45 days as a figure. The Paulo Freire Institute's own chronology has the lessons running from late January to early April 1963; the programme was named for its forty hours of instruction, after which 300 of the 380 who began were certified literate. The entry now says forty hours. Movable Type said Jeremiah Dittmar's estimate put the growth advantage of early-printing cities at 35 percentage points or more. The paper says over 30, and 35 appears nowhere in it. Both figures had been printed under the promise that they were sourced; neither line named where it came from, and both now do.

t: Borlaug's billion and the Jobs paternity test.
b: Norman Borlaug's entry said estimates of the lives the Green Revolution saved run to a billion or more. The figure is repeated everywhere, and the house found no published calculation behind it; the entry on Tu Youyou already refused the same kind of number. It is gone from Borlaug's entry, and his contested section now says the scale is argued rather than measured. Steve Jobs' entry put the probability of paternity at 94.1 per cent, the figure usually cited to Time in 1983, which the house has not opened. Lisa Brennan-Jobs gives 94.4 per cent in her memoir, and the entry now prints hers, with the source named.

t: Bell Labs' Nobels, and a decade nobody measured.
b: Compounding Machines said ten Nobel Prizes had gone to work done at Bell Labs. The documents opened disagree with each other: one list supports ten prize-years from 1937 to 2023, and the article it sits under says eleven. The entry now says at least ten. The same entry printed '~10 yrs' as a figure for PARC's window of influence. It was the house's own arithmetic on two dates, not a number anyone published, and it has been replaced by the date PARC opened.

The Plastic Tide said Richard Thompson coined the word 'microplastics' in 2004, in its opening line, its timeline and its figures. The term appears in marine-pollution work from the 1990s; Thompson's 2004 paper in Science is what put it into circulation. The entry now says that.

Movable Type said presses were operating in about 205 European cities by 1500, out of more than a thousand. Neither number is in the paper the entry relies on; Fernand Braudel's count, the one found, is 236 towns, and the entry now gives his. Cost Disease said New York subway construction runs about $1.5 billion a kilometre. The Transit Costs Project's own New York study puts Phase 1 of the Second Avenue Subway at about $1.7 billion a kilometre, and the entry now says so. In Defense of Bubbles said 85 to 95 per cent of the fibre laid in the 1990s sat dark after the bust. Every account found attributes the range to unnamed analysts, and no study behind it could be opened, so the number is gone.

An audit of claims printed as 'first', 'only' or 'most' found six that said more than a source would. Genghis Khan's entry said he forged the largest contiguous land empire in history; it reached that size under his heirs, after his death in 1227. Rockefeller's called his the largest fortune in American history, with no measure attached; by inflation-adjusted wealth it is not, and by share of the economy it has arguably been overtaken. It now says one of the largest. Edward Thorp's said Beat the Dealer was, by his own description, the first book to prove the house edge could be beaten; his own account of the book does not say so. Why Firms Exist said Coase's paper was largely ignored for thirty years; the paper was cited long before it was put to use, and the entry now quotes only what Coase is on record as saying, that it was little more than an undergraduate essay. Maurice Hilleman's and Fritz Haber's entries stated as the house's own finding what are other people's judgments; both are now worded as such.

t: Five quotations the house had not seen.
b: An audit of quotations checked each one against the document it comes from. Five could not be found in any document the house could open, so they are no longer printed in quotation marks: Confucius on not imposing on others (the translator was never named), Ibn Khaldun on dynasties lasting three generations (not found in the Rosenthal translation the entry relies on), Robert Moses's 'stein' statement (two wordings circulate, and the 1981 obituary that carries it could not be opened), Clair Patterson's 1966 testimony about the Public Health Service, and Thomas Blanton's line about Arkhipov. Each is now given as a paraphrase, which is what the colophon says an unquoted line is. None of them has been shown to be wrong. Separately, Tu Youyou's entry called Rao, Zhang and Li's book the only book-length account in English; Tu's own 2017 book covers the same discovery, as chemistry rather than history.

The Atlas called Mark Bertolini co-CEO of Oscar Health. He is Oscar's chief executive, with effect from 3 April 2023, when the co-founder Mario Schlosser moved to president of technology (Oscar Health press release, 28 March 2023). The co-CEO post he held before that was at Bridgewater Associates.
